hypothesis: Rivet's core bottleneck is not missing tools but missing execution resilience in the agent loop — the correct fix is a TurnHarness abstraction (not full middleware rewrite) that adds retry, trajectory, and implicit task-state.

candidates.oneLiner: Parallel tool execution via isConcurrencySafe() + transient error retry
TurnHarness abstraction + trajectory recording for retry and debug
Prefix-cache-safe implicit planning via task-state injection into volatile context

extinctions.reason: Indirect causality — refactoring doesn't directly improve capability; high cost, high regression risk
salvagedTraits: separation of concerns → harness as lightweight extraction

extinctions.reason: Parallel tool execution depends on unverified DeepSeek multi-tool-use frequency (<5% likely)
salvagedTraits: tool retry logic → integrated into V3 harness

survivors.advantage: Clear causality (retry reduces turn waste), co-evolutionary (trajectory drives continuous improvement), directly reduces loop.ts complexity
Zero API cost planning, leverages existing intent-extractor, prefix-cache-safe

adapt.finalCandidate: V3 + V4 fusion: TurnHarness (execution resilience) + Task State (implicit planning)
adapt.convergenceInsight: Execution resilience is not about 'what to do after failure' but 'giving the model enough execution state information at every turn to make correct decisions'

implementationPhases.action: Extract TurnHarness from loop.ts + add tool retry for transient errors
Trajectory recording + task-state extraction + volatile context injection

fragments.text: OpenClaw is a gateway-centric always-on platform, not a CLI agent — its patterns are transferable but not its features
OpenClaw's AgentHarness decouples execution from orchestration, enabling hot-swap of providers
OpenClaw trajectory recording is separate from session transcript — enables debug without polluting context
OpenClaw tool availability expressions: declarative allOf/anyOf conditions eliminate scattered runtime checks
OpenClaw model fallback with cooldown probes: tracks per-model failure cooldowns, periodically probes recovery
loop.ts is 411 lines with run() at 240 lines — already a God Method with 8+ orthogonal concerns
DeepSeek V4 multi-tool-use frequency is unverified — parallel tool execution may be <5% utilization
Planning turn breaks prefix cache stability — implicit planning via volatile context injection is cache-safe
Reflexion pattern: agent generates self-reflection after failure, retries with reflection as context
Error classification (transient/recoverable/permanent) + graded response is industry best practice
TDD closed loop: write test → run → fail → fix → run → pass — agent as test-driven developer
Existing failure-classifier.ts already classifies 8 failure modes — can be extended to drive retry decisions
isConcurrencySafe() interface exists in tool registry but loop.ts never consumes it
Checkpoint is per-session single snapshot, not per-tool — cannot precisely rollback one failed tool in parallel scenario
